conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states 'Conclusion: Supported' and provides strong evidence from clinical trials and FDA approval confirming that abaloparatide significantly reduces vertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: Supported.** Abaloparatide significantly reduces the risk of new vertebral fractures (as well as nonvertebral fractures) in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

**Evidence:**
The pivotal Phase 3 ACTIVE trial—a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis—found that 18 months of subcutaneous abaloparatide significantly reduced new vertebral and nonvertebral fractures compared with placebo (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27533157/; https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640). This effect was consistent across prespecified high-risk subgroups (defined by prior fracture, low BMD, or elevated FRAX score) and persisted through the 43-month ACTIVE–ACTIVExtend extension study (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916366/).

This body of evidence formed the basis for FDA approval, and the official Tymlos (abaloparatide) prescribing label explicitly states that the drug "reduces the risk of vertebral... fractures" in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, with consistent benefit regardless of age, years since menopause, prior fracture status, or baseline bone mineral density (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf).

Independent network meta-analyses comparing abaloparatide to other osteoporosis therapies and placebo have corroborated these findings, confirming statistically significant reductions in vertebral fracture risk (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332256197_Abaloparatide_for_risk_reduction_of_nonvertebral_and_vertebral_fractures_in_postmenopausal_women_with_osteoporosis_a_network_meta-analysis).

**Overall:** The claim is well-supported by high-quality randomized controlled trial data (ACTIVE/ACTIVExtend), regulatory review (FDA label), and independent meta-analyses, all converging on the same conclusion: abaloparatide reduces vertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, particularly those at high baseline fracture risk.
